items.title: Christopher "Happy" Goldston Interview, 1959-01-13
items.q: Well, Amos Riley picked me out to play drum in his orchestra. And that's the first good band I ever played with. And I joined Amos's band.

ctx.x: Is that Tom Benton? Did you know Tom Benton, by the way? You introduced me to Tom Benton.

Yeah, I used to play with Tom Benton. Yeah, years ago, me and Tom played together. And so, getting back to the... Is that the telephone? No, no, I didn't hear my ring. Oh. And getting back to the old musicians came to us. Used to come to our rehearsal. Well, they used to come around, and they used to hear us, and they would help us out. And they would help us out. You know, it was a little, like, like, Dick Chambers, Amos Riley. All those old ones, at that time, used to come around. Mm-hm. You were talking Amos…
Oh, yes, the two-lane band. The brass band. The brass band. Who was in the dance band with him when you played for dancers?

items.title: Christopher "Happy" Goldston Interview, 1962-04-11
items.q: And Amos took me. And he had a brass band that called two-lane band. And was putting me in the two-lane band.

ctx.x: Well, I was just playing around, you know. But I wasn't playing out, you know. I was mostly playing drumming. Yeah. They used two pieces. They used the hard part. And I used to play those. Now the old Ringo band I started out with playing. And what put me on the market is Amos Raleigh. And that's the two-lane band. He was the one who picked me up. And I played with Amos. Ooh, a long time. And Amos took me. And he had a brass band that called two-lane band. And was putting me in the two-lane band. That's the same…
And the main sound was the drum. Because they had to have Kato.
